reason: The passage explicitly demonstrates a failure of leadership accountability, most strikingly in Eli's case. In 1 Samuel 3:13, God states through Samuel: 'וְהִגַּדְתִּי לוֹ כִּֽי־ שֹׁפֵט אֲנִי אֶת־ בֵּיתוֹ עַד־ עוֹלָם בַּעֲוֺן אֲשֶׁר־ יָדַע כִּֽי־ מְקַֽלְלִים לָהֶם בָּנָיו וְלֹא כִהָה בָּם' (I will judge his house forever because of the iniquity which he knew, because his sons were cursing God, and he did not restrain them). Eli's knowledge combined with inaction ('וְלֹא כִהָה בָּם' - he did not restrain them) explicitly shows a leader who failed to take accountability for the moral corruption within his own house. Furthermore, when Israel's military situation deteriorates against the Philistines, the elders seek to remedy the crisis by bringing the Ark of the Covenant, suggesting reliance on symbolic religious objects rather than addressing the underlying spiritual and moral failures of their leadership.
